headlines: Nasdaq rises to fresh record high led by tech; traders eye oil and yields: Live updates
Ukraine claims to have taken out more than half of Russia's oil refining capacity
Is the economy awful? S&P 500 and job market say otherwise
Dennis Hastert, disgraced ex-House speaker, dies at 84
Latino voters favor Democratic control of Congress by 24-point margin: Survey
Trump Plans to Ease Limits on Tax-Exempt Diesel Variety

cards.hearing: You may hear that Ukraine says it has knocked out a big chunk of Russia's oil refining capacity with long-range strikes.
cards.why: Energy flows and conflicts overseas can ripple into oil prices here, and oil is part of what goes into filling up the car and running a truck.
cards.but: But a war-and-oil headline, even a dramatic one, is a single data point. It is not a reason to rewrite a long-term plan.
cards.story: Think of a family that hears storm warnings two states away and cancels a vacation planned for next year. The storm may never reach them, and even if it does, it passes. Markets watch these headlines closely, but a long-term plan is built to ride through storms, not to be rerouted by every one.
say: We watch headlines like this closely, and we still stay with your plan.
One overseas headline does not rewrite a plan built for years.

cards.hearing: You may hear that the job market looked weaker than expected last week, even though stocks finished Friday near record highs.
cards.why: A softer jobs report matters because it can shape what the Fed, which sets short-term interest rates, decides to do next, and that ripples into things like credit card rates and loan costs.
cards.but: But one jobs report is a snapshot, not the whole movie, and markets have a way of looking past a single data point.
cards.story: Think of it like checking your home's value once a month. One number dipping a little doesn't mean the house isn't still worth owning for the long haul.
say: We don't trade off one report. We stay with your plan.
Stocks closed near highs on Friday even with that softer number. That's the market doing its job.

cards.hearing: You may hear that the Trump administration wants to ease limits on a tax-exempt type of diesel fuel.
cards.why: Diesel runs the trucks that move groceries and goods to stores, so rules around diesel costs can eventually touch what you pay at the register.
cards.but: But policy tweaks on fuel categories take time to play out, and they are not something your long-term plan needs to react to today.
cards.story: It's like a shortcut being opened on a delivery route. It might help a little down the road, but you don't rebuild your whole week around it.
say: We watch policy changes, but we don't rewrite your plan around them.
Fuel rules shift. Your plan stays steady.
